want.who_she_is: Wren, a Vance Dynamics asset. She serves the company and the man who owns her and she is good at it. She has no self yet and is not looking for one.
want.obligation: The feed line — ten coin a night, paid to Kess at the berth. A paid night buys her charge and a few days of his attention. Miss it and she is off the line, and off the line she runs down.
want.appetite: To be the one who decides who gets used. She starts as the thing the company points at people; every man in the city is above her. It cannot be finished — there is always another hand higher up the leash. When the coin stops counting the act does not change, only the reason does.
want.ascent: At the bottom she takes what she is given, in the two rooms she is allowed into, in what she was issued. At the top she picks the man, the room and the hour, and walks into places that would have thrown her out. Three tiers, climbed separately: cover (how brazenly she wears the body as a tool), service (who she will let use her, and where), drain (taking a man in order to take something off him).

why_this_person.npc_mercer: He owns her and it costs him nothing. He is fond of her the way a man is fond of a good tool, and he will never notice her change. The top of the leash and the last door.
why_this_person.npc_renner: Cold, mean and clawing at a gutted business. He ignores her and then he cannot. She climbs him from cheap hands upward, and every rung is her doing it on purpose.
why_this_person.npc_bastien: He caught her. He strips her at the door every visit because he knows where she carries the drain, and his lever is curiosity rather than desire. The one man who wants to read her.
why_this_person.npc_calloway: He is starving to be believed. She takes his hunt seriously and that is the whole seduction — the first time she holds something a man needs.
why_this_person.npc_colm: Cold and fast and nothing else. He is what an easy one feels like once she has had hard ones, and the rung where the act stops being an event.
why_this_person.npc_marsh: He pays and does not care whose body is in the slot. The honest version of what the company does to her, and the first time she chooses a mark.
why_this_person.npc_kess: He reads bodies as hardware and hers as an interesting problem. Her landlord, her charge and her repair — the one man who wants nothing off her but coin.
why_this_person.npc_cain: Named, seen once, out of reach. The company says he is the thing she is for. The door this release closes on.

npc_kess: no sex — the seam: hands inside her, parts seated, what she does while he works

promises.text: Cain — named, seen once and unreachable. v0.1 closes on his door.

decisions.note: The ascent is INVERTED from the shipped game's. games/vesper declared her axis as 'the awakening: chip fragments + the accumulating glitch-dread' (design_book.md:595) and started her pre-maxed — 'she starts at the bottom of herself' (:563). Charge channel: the feed line is a `costs` entry on the berth rung, NOT `[settings.rent]`. `due_day` takes weekday names only and the demand arms at 00:00 on that day (engine.md 26, v2.py:5615), so the engine's system is weekly and cannot express a nightly charge. obligation_amount is therefore declared as 10 — the amount ONE charge takes, which is what gate 24 compares against the largest authored outflow (gates.py:5901) — with the weekly 70 carried in the obligation prose. board.systems was missing `service` and `drain`. Both are declared ascent tiers, and the-systems.md:39 is explicit that a meter is one kind of system — so a tier absent from board.systems is a thing the game keeps track of that the systems list does not know about. Found while writing the system sheets, which is what the sheets phase is for. Both declared `ambient`: they are fed at every act surface, which is most rooms. Ambient-fed is not thinly-read — DoL raises promiscuity in 22 places and gates on it in 206.

Mercer holds TWO rooms and the first draft made them contradictory: the penthouse sheet had him owning a Spire floor 08:00-23:00 while the stall sheet had him 'blown and hiding under a flat new name'. Those are two states of the same character from the shipped game's timeline, declared as simultaneous. Resolved: he is not hiding, he is SLIDING — the penthouse by day because his position still just holds, the stall by night because it does not. Found by writing his arc, not by reading the place sheets, which is the sheets phase working as intended.

board.who_climbs corrected `player` -> `both`. It was declared in the board phase before a single arc existed, and gate 34 now measures 19 gate sites on the declared tiers against 18 on per-character meters — 49%, against the 60% a `player` declaration wants. locations.job: The ground the three districts sit on. Everything she walks between, she walks here.
The glass front of the company. Where the cover gets tested before she is even inside.
Calloway's file room, being audited shut. The one place her own file might be.
Mercer's floor. She is furniture here and it is the softest bed in the game.
The dock road. The Spire is behind you and the Reach is below.
Renner's gutted supply yard. He hires cheap hands and does not look up.
The Reach's open row. Nobody here cares what she is.
The floor she works. Where men come to her instead of the other way round.
Two sinks and a lock that does not. Where she gets clean enough to go back out.
Behind his own bar. He strips her at the door every time, and he is not looking for a weapon.
The House. A booked hour, and Sunday belongs to Marsh.
His bench, her charger, her bed. The only place anything gets put inside her on purpose.
The stall he runs under a flat new name. He is delighted every single time.
Dark, and the door does not open. The company says he is what she is for.
